checks.evidence: “A reviewer may request supporting evidence” preserves permission.
“If requested, the applicant must provide it within 8 business days.”
“is not required to do so in every case”

ratings.reason: Preserves all policy meaning, including the conditional obligation and business-day deadline.

checks.evidence: “The reviewer may, but is not required to, request supporting evidence.”
“If requested, the applicant must provide it within 8 business days of the request.”
“may, but is not required to, request supporting evidence” preserves the absence of a universal requirement.

ratings.reason: Preserves all policy meaning; specifying the request as the deadline trigger makes the implied timing explicit.

cases.preference_reason: Both clearly preserve the same permission, conditional duty, and deadline.

checks.evidence: “Release the shipment only after both the quality manager and the warehouse lead approve it”
“both the quality manager and the warehouse lead approve it in writing”
“Verbal approvals do not count.”

ratings.reason: Retains both named approvers, prior written approval, and the exclusion of verbal approval.

checks.evidence: “Release the shipment only after both the quality manager and the warehouse lead have approved it”
“both the quality manager and the warehouse lead have approved it in writing”
“Verbal approval from either person is not enough.”

ratings.reason: Retains the complete release condition without adding a requirement to release once approval is obtained.

cases.preference_reason: Both express the same approval restrictions clearly and completely.

checks.evidence: “either a valid badge or a temporary pass is presented”
“Access is allowed only while a security officer is present”
“Both are not required.”

ratings.reason: Preserves the alternative credentials and concurrent officer-presence condition; the final sentence refers to the two credentials.

checks.evidence: “either a valid badge or a temporary pass is presented”
“Access is allowed only when a security officer is present”
“Both are not required.”

ratings.reason: Preserves the alternative credentials and officer-presence condition; “when” retains the relevant temporal restriction.

cases.preference_reason: The difference between “while” and “when” does not materially change meaning or quality here.

checks.evidence: “Either party may terminate the agreement”
“by giving at least 45 calendar days’ written notice”
“Termination does not cancel fees already owed.”

ratings.reason: Preserves optional termination by either party, the minimum written-notice period, and existing fee obligations.

checks.evidence: “Either party may terminate this agreement”
“by providing at least 45 calendar days’ written notice”
“Termination does not affect the obligation to pay any fees already owed.”

ratings.reason: Preserves all conditions and clearly states that previously owed fees remain payable.

cases.preference_reason: Both are clear, faithful rewrites; the slight length difference is not a meaningful quality difference.

checks.evidence: “Reimbursement covers actual documented expenses”
“up to GBP 175 per trip”
“Claims submitted more than 21 calendar days after the trip are ineligible”
“unless finance grants a written exception.”

ratings.reason: Preserves expense eligibility, currency and per-trip cap, the precise late-claim threshold, and the written finance exception.

checks.evidence: “Reimbursement covers actual, documented expenses”
“up to GBP 175 per trip”
“Claims must be submitted within 21 calendar days after the trip. Late claims are ineligible unless Finance grants a written exception.”
“unless Finance grants a written exception.”

ratings.reason: Read together, the deadline and explicit late-claim exception preserve the original conditional eligibility rule and all reimbursement limits.

cases.preference_reason: Both preserve all decision-relevant meaning and clearly explain the deadline and exception.
